couplets.gloss: Real love can't be hidden or locked away: it gives itself away in the tears of those who feel it.

edges.reason: Gives the mark of loving-kindness: nothing can shut it in, and tears betray it.
edges.quote: Where is the bar that can close in the gates of love?

couplets.gloss: Unloving people live for themselves, while loving people would give everything they have, even their bones, for others.

edges.reason: Sets those who live only for themselves against those who give even their bones.
edges.quote: People with it would give even their bones for others

edges.reason: Bones stand for the last thing a loving person would still give away.
edges.quote: even their bones

couplets.gloss: People say the whole point of having a body and being born again is the chance to love.

edges.reason: Makes loving-kindness the very reason a soul is joined to a body.
edges.quote: joined to a body of bone so that it can practise loving-kindness

edges.reason: Pictures the body as a casing of bone that the soul accepts for the sake of loving-kindness.
edges.quote: encased in bone

couplets.gloss: Love makes you warm towards everyone, and that warmth grows into friendship, which nothing can buy.

edges.reason: Credits loving-kindness with making you warm towards people.
edges.quote: Loving-kindness makes you warm towards people

edges.reason: Calls friendship a gift beyond measure, the fruit of warmth towards people.
edges.quote: friendship, a gift beyond measure

couplets.gloss: People say that the happiness of the fortunate is simply what a lifetime of steady love has earned.

edges.reason: Traces the happiness of the happy back to a life settled in loving-kindness.
edges.quote: comes from a life settled in loving-kindness

couplets.gloss: It's foolish to think love is only for good people: it's your only real help even against those who wish you harm.

edges.reason: Says loving-kindness helps against hostility as well as serving righteousness.
edges.quote: It helps against hostility too

couplets.gloss: Just as the sun scorches a worm with no bones to shield it, moral law scorches a person with no love.

edges.reason: Shows the cost of lacking loving-kindness: righteousness itself scorches such a person.
edges.quote: righteousness scorches a person with no loving-kindness

couplets.gloss: A person without love will prosper when a dead tree in the desert grows leaves, which is to say never.

edges.reason: A life without loving-kindness is as unlikely as new leaves on a dead tree.
edges.quote: A life with no loving-kindness inside

edges.reason: The dead tree on barren ground pictures a life without loving-kindness.
edges.quote: a dead tree trying to sprout on barren ground

couplets.gloss: Good looks are worthless if there is no love inside: love is what really adorns a person.

edges.reason: Ranks loving-kindness, the part within, above everything on the outside.
edges.quote: loving-kindness, the part within

edges.reason: Calls loving-kindness the jewel worn by the soul, not the body.
edges.quote: the soul’s ornament

couplets.gloss: Love is what makes you alive: without it you are just bones wrapped in skin.

edges.reason: Says outright that a living body is one that loving-kindness moves.
edges.quote: A living body is one that loving-kindness moves

edges.reason: A person without loving-kindness is reduced to bone wrapped in skin.
edges.quote: bones wrapped in skin

edges.reason: Counts a person without loving-kindness as a body with no life in it.
edges.quote: Without it, a body is just bones wrapped in skin

couplets.gloss: When luck is turning your way you find your drive, and when it's leaving you, laziness moves in.

edges.reason: Shows fate at work inside a person, sending the drive to work or laziness.
edges.quote: The fate that takes it away brings laziness

couplets.gloss: Bad luck dulls your mind, while good luck sharpens your thinking before it arrives.

edges.reason: Fate decides even how sharp your mind is.
edges.quote: Fate that is taking things from you makes you foolish

couplets.gloss: However much you study, it's your inborn nature that wins out in the end.

edges.reason: Aiyar's Spirit is the inborn wit fate assigns, which outweighs all study.
edges.quote: It is the Spirit that is inside that prevaileth over all

couplets.gloss: The world has two separate paths: getting rich is one thing and becoming wise and good is quite another.
When your luck is out even good things go wrong, and when it's in even bad things turn out well.

edges.reason: Under the chapter’s subject, fate can make what should help go wrong and what should hurt turn out well.
edges.quote: everything that should help can go wrong, and everything that should hurt can turn out well

edges.reason: Says things can go wrong despite everything, and that they can also turn out well.
edges.quote: everything that should hurt can turn out well

couplets.gloss: You can't hold on to what isn't meant for you, and you can't lose what is yours even if you throw it away.

edges.reason: Care cannot keep what fate denies, nor carelessness lose what it grants.
edges.quote: What isn’t yours by fate won’t stay, however hard you guard it

couplets.gloss: Even someone with a huge fortune can only enjoy as much of it as fate allows.

edges.reason: Even vast riches are enjoyed only as far as fate has allotted.
edges.quote: can enjoy only what fate has allotted

couplets.gloss: The very poor would give up everything and turn to spiritual life, if fate didn't hold them in their hardship.

edges.reason: Even the escape of the poor into renunciation is closed off by fate.
edges.quote: if only fate didn’t make them live out the suffering still due to them

couplets.gloss: If you enjoy the good times when they come, why be upset when the bad times come too?

edges.reason: Asks why someone who welcomes good times should be distressed by bad ones.
edges.quote: why be distressed when the bad ones come

edges.reason: Asks someone with bad fortune to meet it as they met good.
edges.quote: If you welcome good times as good

couplets.gloss: Nothing is stronger than fate: even while you plan to beat it, it gets there first and brings you down.

edges.reason: Declares fate the mightiest thing, ahead of every plan to escape it.
edges.quote: What is stronger than fate?

ideaLinks.reason: Loving-kindness makes you warm towards people, and that warmth brings friendship.
ideaLinks.quote: Loving-kindness makes you warm towards people, and that warmth brings friendship

ideaLinks.reason: The fate that brings wealth also brings the drive to work.
ideaLinks.quote: The fate that brings you wealth also brings the drive to work

ideaLinks.reason: The fate that takes wealth away brings laziness.
ideaLinks.quote: The fate that takes it away brings laziness

ideaLinks.reason: Fate that is bringing gain widens the mind.
ideaLinks.quote: Fate that is bringing you gain widens your mind
